title: In silico and Network Pharmacology Identification of Acacia senegal Phytochemicals as Potential alpha-Amylase Inhibitors.
authors: Abdu, Abdulkadir; Bakrey, Hossamaldeen; Rikabi, Hind A; Ali, Amani Ahmed Osman; Abdelrahim, Israa; Abdulkareem, Eman M; Eltaib, Lina
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子对接、DFT和MD模拟筛选金合欢植物化合物作为α-淀粉酶抑制剂，对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA体系，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Diabetes mellitus is a rapidly expanding chronic disease, prompting interest in plant-derived natural products as adjuncts to conventional therapy because of their improvements in glycaemic control and reduced complications. To evaluate phytochemicals' potential as alpha-amylase inhibitors using an integrated in-silico workflow. METHODS: Acacia senegal phytochemicals retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 database were evaluated their in-silico studies against alpha-amylase inhibitors using molecular docking, DFT, pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiling, in addition to PASS prediction, network pharmacology and MD simulations. RESULTS: Docking of 31 compounds was carried out, and the top three ligands, which are: IMPHY014840 (-9.321 kcal/mol), IMPHY014838 (-9.208 kcal/mol) and IMPHY006972 (-9.026 kcal/mol), were selected. Their favorable binding energies indicated strong predicted affinity toward the selected enzyme target. DFT calculations showed identical HOMO-LUMO gaps of 6.936 eV for the first two ligands, whereas the third one displayed a larger gap of 9.484 eV, indicating lower chemical reactivity. Furthermore, pharmacokinetic screening indicated high human intestinal absorption (75-86 %) and favorable Caco-2 permeability for the top three compounds, particularly for IMPHY014840 and IMPHY014838. PASS analysis suggested protease target affinity for IMPHY014840 and GPCR/transcription factor activity for IMPHY014838, expanding their therapeutic scope beyond alpha-amylase inhibition. MD trajectories confirmed overall complex stability, with IMPHY014838 exhibiting marginally lower ligand RMSD and therefore slightly superior dynamical stability. DISCUSSION: The present study identified IMPHY014840 and IMPHY014838 as promising alpha- amylase inhibitors, with docking scores of -9.321 and -9.208 kcal/mol, respectively. DFT, ADMET, toxicity, PASS, and 100 ns MD simulations indicate stable enzyme-ligand binding, high predicted intestinal absorption, and multitarget potential. Network pharmacology further suggests that these compounds act on a broad set of diabetes related targets, supporting their value as antidiabetic lead candidates. CONCLUSION: The combined computational evidence supports IMPHY014840 and IMPHY014838 as promising natural alpha-amylase inhibitors for type 2 DM management, and recommends in vitro, in vivo, and formulation optimization to address their limitations.
abstract_zh: 引言：糖尿病是一种快速增长的慢性疾病，促使人们对植物来源的天然产物作为常规疗法的辅助手段产生兴趣，因为它们能改善血糖控制并减少并发症。本研究旨在利用整合的计算机模拟工作流程评估植物化学物质作为α-淀粉酶抑制剂（alpha-amylase inhibitors）的潜力。方法：从IMPPAT 2.0数据库中检索阿拉伯胶（Acacia senegal）的植物化学物质，通过分子对接（molecular docking）、DFT、药代动力学和毒性分析，以及PASS预测、网络药理学和分子动力学（MD）模拟，评估其对α-淀粉酶抑制剂的计算机模拟研究。结果：对31种化合物进行了对接，选出了前三个配体，即IMPHY014840（-9.321 kcal/mol）、IMPHY014838（-9.208 kcal/mol）和IMPHY006972（-9.026 kcal/mol）。它们有利的结合能表明对所选酶靶点具有强预测亲和力。DFT计算显示前两个配体的HOMO-LUMO能隙相同，为6.936 eV，而第三个配体显示出更大的能隙9.484 eV，表明其化学反应性较低。此外，药代动力学筛选显示，前三种化合物具有高人体肠道吸收率（75-86%）和有利的Caco-2渗透性，尤其是IMPHY014840和IMPHY014838。PASS分析提示IMPHY014840具有蛋白酶靶点亲和力，IMPHY014838具有GPCR/转录因子活性，将其治疗范围扩展到α-淀粉酶抑制之外。MD轨迹确认了整体复合物稳定性，其中IMPHY014838表现出略低的配体RMSD，因此动态稳定性略优。讨论：本研究确定IMPHY014840和IMPHY014838为有前景的α-淀粉酶抑制剂，对接分数分别为-9.321和-9.208 kcal/mol。DFT、ADMET、毒性、PASS和100 ns MD模拟表明酶-配体结合稳定、预测肠道吸收率高且具有多靶点潜力。网络药理学进一步表明，这些化合物作用于广泛的糖尿病相关靶点，支持其作为抗糖尿病先导候选物的价值。结论：综合计算证据支持IMPHY014840和IMPHY014838作为治疗2型糖尿病的有前景的天然α-淀粉酶抑制剂，并建议进行体外、体内和制剂优化以解决其局限性。
